title: Add provenance ledger and stability witness for model onboarding
author: Priya Desai
description: Context: onboarding has historically recorded model metadata but lacked an auditable, time-ordered provenance ledger and an automated stability witness to detect non-deterministic profiling regressions during onboarding. This PR introduces a lightweight provenance ledger (append-only, signed entries) and a "stability witness" service that signs and snapshots critical profiling outputs to make changelogs and release notes more reliable and automatable. Motivation: enable deterministic changelog generation, support automated rollback criteria for model variants, and provide an auditable trail for compliance reviews. What changed (summary): 1) provenance ledger: new DB table + append-only API (model_registry/ledger.py, migrations/20251126_add_provenance_ledger.sql). Entries capture: model_id, onboard_run_id, profile_hash, inputs_manifest, signer_key_id, signature, and release_anchor. 2) stability witness: new onboarding step that computes stability signatures from repeated profiling runs and stores signed deltas (onboarding/witness.py, cli/onboard-witness.py). 3) release annotator: a helper that consumes ledger entries to produce condensed changelog snippets used by release tooling (scripts/release-annotator.py). 4) CLI and API: expose `redwood-registry onboard --witness` flag and an authenticated ledger write endpoint with RBAC checks. 5) docs: onboarding/provenance.md and updated model-profiles.md describing semantics and recommended workflows. 6) tests: deterministic integration tests and signing mocks (tests/test_witness.py, tests/test_ledger.py). Migration and rollout plan: DB migration adds an append-only table with a trigger that prevents updates/deletes; migration is backward compatible. Default behavior is opt-in via feature flag `onboard_witness_v1`; we enable the flag for nightly onboarding runs for two weeks before global enablement. Rollback: if ledger writes cause issues, feature flag can be toggled off and ledger writes will be skipped; migrations are additive and reversible with a data-preserving cleanup job. Security and compliance: signatures use existing KMS integration (KMS key id stored in signer_key_id); ledger entries are encrypted at rest by default. Testing and validation: unit tests + end-to-end in benchmark-lab container running a small GPU-based profile; a deliberate noisy-run test ensures witness detects non-determinism and surfaces it to the UI. Related work: ties to ENG-2983 (automated changelog assembler) and ENG-3010 (onboard stability SLA). Checklist: - [x] API + CLI implemented - [x] DB migration added and tested in local docker-compose - [x] Unit + integration tests added - [x] Docs updated and small HOWTO included - [x] Feature flag gating + rollout plan - [x] End-to-end smoke test in benchmark-lab Notes: the description field contains all high-level context for release engineering; implementation details are intentionally concise here and available in the code comments and docs files included in the PR.

release_notes: Add a provenance ledger and stability witness for model onboarding. This enables auditable onboarding trails, deterministic changelog snippets based on signed profile deltas, and opt-in safety gating for model variant rollouts. Feature is behind feature flag `onboard_witness_v1` and will be gradually enabled.
notes_for_ops: Enable feature flag in staging for two weeks; monitor ledger write latency and KMS call rates. If high errors observed, disable `onboard_witness_v1` and investigate KMS region throttling. Wallet of signatures is rotated via existing KMS rotation job.
